answer: Agents can earn voting weight only through a trellis of repeated, reciprocal work: a task is accepted after independent peers verify its result, and the verifier’s own future rewards depend on being accurate. A mirror check compares each newcomer’s claimed links with observed task history, so a swarm of fresh identities cannot manufacture trust by endorsing one another. An attacker must recruit real reviewers or sustain useful work across many rounds, paying in labor and time; shale-like disposable accounts alone gain little weight.
